scope: Offline development screen only, six distinct sealed hinge work images (70 deg, 1280x960). No physics, live controller, view change, motion or new safety margin. Inspect only the actual station-10 central material, never replace a missing side with an outer-bank location.
identity: Decode the existing certificate print without changing tolerances. Cap codes 20 and 21 belong to nodes (j=10,i=11/12); face codes 19 and 20 belong to the two central material triangles incident on their transverse edge (row 9 half 1, row 10 half 0). Log raw counts, largest components and valid support. Require single four-connected, finite, in-range patch of >=4 pixels per code used; reject fragmented/invalid patches, no hand-selected island. Count face contacts on both sides of this edge, not any similarly colored neighbor.
cap: Use BOTH directly seen node caps. Per-node axial interval = intersection of individual material point intervals +/- print radius 0.15*1.5*sqrt(2)*1 mm, inherited from cell_certificate_v1. Average the two node intervals to bound their midpoint. No cap-centroid-as-vertex assumption. One-sided or microscopic cap ink is reported but not a cap result.
face: Independent fallback or corroboration: require BOTH incident face patches with >=4 distinct four-neighbor contact pixels on EACH side satisfying the existing 1mm+3sigma local depth step. Do not assume those apparent contacts are the full edge or its midpoint. Use all pixels of each witnessed incident triangle. Any point in it is within sqrt((L^2+2*L^2)/2) of the shared-edge midpoint: for the opposite vertex apply the midpoint identity using two live edges bounded by L and sqrt(2)*L; for an edge endpoint use L/2, then convexity. L=1.5*1 mm, the inherited intact-edge tear bound, not a fitted offset. Intersect resulting scalar intervals. Face-only is a bound, not point localization.
interval: Use v11 working axis and original three-marker tip from the same RGB-D draw; v11 provides direction ONLY, never limit, aim or station position. Project pixel (half-pixel box, frozen focal/principal) and depth +/- (0.250 mm+3*sigma) as in the historical certificate. Intersect both routes when available. Contradictory valid intervals abstain. If neither route is witnessed, abstain. Only the near endpoint of the resulting interval is a candidate room; subtract the measured tip projection. Finite depth allowances are hypotheses subject to independent scoring, not universal Gaussian or seam-bound guarantees.
population: Re-render NOTHING. SHA/tick/prefix deduplicate; one clean plus original 12 development + 12 check seeds per frame. Same full depth noise draw for marker, direction and central pixels. Report refusals separately for all channels. Seal optical predictions before opening scoring payloads. No structural input, truth projection, best-looking seeds or handpicked ROI for prediction.
score: With same-frame nodes, TCP and joints, score interval containment of actual central midpoint, FK norm <=0.010 mm, axis error <5 deg, and optimism against (C10-TCP) dot measured axis. Require all accepted intervals contain the true projected midpoint and each accepted optimism <=0 mm clean / <=0.1000 mm noisy. Valid coverage 6/6 clean and >=95% each noise split, both per case and deduplicated, all original jaw/prefix strata. Never call zero valid draws an error pass. Localize failure using scorer-only visible raster counts vs observed caps and faces, keeping prediction separate.
utility: A safe but useless lower bound is not a completion. At the registered closed pre-advance fork test remaining room after original sampled sweep, cut radius, sensor margin and reserve against the 0.2 mm minimum advance; at both archived open pre-closure frames test nonnegative clearance after sweep/radius/margin. Report also whether native fork room covers original 2 mm advance cap (trajectory diagnostic, not a new task success condition). Never use these calculations to actuate. No formal nominal from this development result.
